newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends at 7-year low, BOK sells dlrs.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends at 7-year low, BOK sells dlrs.

text.p: The won closed at a seven-year low against the dollar on Monday as the nation's widening trade deficit fuelled demand for the U.S. unit, dealers said.
The Bank of Korea intervened in early morning trade to support the local currency, but the won ended at 887.80, the lowest closing since the nation launched the market average system in March 1990.
In early morning trade, the central bank offered to sell dollars at 899.00 won in the three-month forward trading and at 913.00 in the six-month forward trading.
The won opened at 886.00 and touched an interday low of 887.90. It closed at 884.90 on Friday.
Dealers said the won's weakness stemmed from the nation's widening trade deficit and the reopening of a prosecution probe into a loan scandal involving Hanbo Steel Co.
"The dollar's strength is expected to continue for the time being," a domestic bank dealer said.
Dealers said the central bank offered to sell about $300 million for three-month forward trading and all the amount was contracted immediately.
